trigger: disk-pressure or transient I/O error occurring after ofstream::operator<< returns but before the block-scope destructor's implicit flush/close, which cannot propagate the error
summary: REQUIRE(f.good()) after the ofstream << write only proves bytes were accepted into the internal streambuf, not that they reached disk; the real flush happens in the destructor at scope exit, which swallows any I/O error, so a disk-pressure scenario could still silently leave a 0-byte file for CommandDedupStore::open() to accept as a fresh valid empty DB.
classification: truth-adjacent test-quality finding, not a wording issue
